newsitem.title: UK: UK to take reserve powers on stamp duty.
newsitem.headline: UK to take reserve powers on stamp duty.

text.p: Chancellor of the Exchequer Kenneth Clarke said on Thursday he planned to take reserve powers to impose stamp duty on certain share purchases and other transactions by intermediaries in the London stock market.
"These powers could be activated to prevent against loss of revenue arising from abuse of the extended relief for intermediaries' transactions," Clarke said in a written parliamentary answer.

The potential revenue losses could occur when current stamp duty exemptions for market makers and brokers on the London Stock Exchange are replaced by a new system of relief for market intermediaries, he said.
Clarke said he expected the proposed new regime would deliver broadly the same revenue from stamp duty as the current one.

The expectation was based on the fact that the government had decided not to "confine the relief available to intermediaries (under the new system) to purchases which are offset by sales within a given period."

"The introduction of such a time limit would impose additional compliance cost on firms, it would encourage a new type of tax-driven trading, and it would do little if anything to protect the revenue from stamp trading on shares," he said.
Clarke said the proposed new regime would also replace existing stamp duty reliefs for traders on the London International Financial Futures and Options Exchange (LIFFE).

"Detailed provisions reflecting these proposals will be brought forward for the 1997 Finance Bill with a view to implementing the new regime as soon as is practicable during the course of 1997-8," he said.
